account lists `needsReconnect: true` and keeps its id until the next\n upload restores it.\n* **Uploads are budgeted** per person

### Who can upload

An API key
acts as the person who created it, with all of that person's\naccess. For personal accounts, upload with the key of a dedicated me
mber who\nis not a project admin, so a leaked CI key can't do an admin's work. On a\nserver shared with the project, accounts are

project accounts: only a project
admin can upload, rename or delete them, and every member's hosted runs can
use them.

### Ru

nning evals as an account

A run with no saved account choice acts as the server's **default** account.
To run evals from CI as

one account, upload its token, make it the default,
then start the run:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
curl -fs
S -X PATCH \\\n \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/accounts/test-automation-1\" \\\n -H \"A

uthorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{ "isDefault": true }'
```

The
CLI takes the same steps with `mcpjam cloud server-accounts set`, which\nreads the token from a file, an environment variable or s
tdin, and\n`mcpjam cloud server-accounts default`. See the\n[CLI reference](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference.md#cloud-server-

accounts-commands).

The default is shared by every run that key starts, so don't run the same
key's runs at the same time with
different defaults. Where your organization\nhas account choice for eval suites, a suite can instead save the accounts it\nruns a

s, in its settings in the app; a run with a saved choice uses those
accounts and ignores the default.

### Deleting an account\
n\n`DELETE` removes the account and its stored token, and asks the token's issuer\nto revoke the token where the issuer supports r
evocation. That is best effort,\nand it also ends any copy of the same token you still hold. The default\naccount can't be deleted

while other accounts exist (`409`): make another
account the default first.

### The deprecated import route

`POST .../oaut
h/import-tokens` still works, and is removed 90 days after the\naccounts API shipped. It uploads to your default account, creating
an unnamed\none when the server has none, and keeps its old body and its old\n`{ imported, expiresAt }` answer. Every answer carr

ies `Deprecation: true`, a
`Sunset` date and a `Link` to `.../accounts`.

An account this route creates is hosted-only. An exis
ting default it writes\ninto keeps whatever rule it had. Its `serverUrl` must be the URL saved in the\nproject, or the answer is `
400`. `authorizationServerUrl`, `oauthResourceUrl`\nand `tokens.id_token` are accepted and ignored. Move to\n`PUT .../accounts/{ac

count}`, which names the account it writes.

The error codes these routes add to `details.code` are listed in the
[error code r

eference](https://docs.mcpjam.com/troubleshooting/error-codes.md#server-account-errors).

## Run evals from the API

The short

ROJECT_ID/eval-runs\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\" \\\n -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n -d '{\n

"suiteName": "smoke",
 "serverIds": ["'$SERVER_ID'"],
 "tests": [{
 "title": "echo works",

"runs": 1,
 "model": "anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5",
 "provider": "anthropic",
 "steps": [
 {

"kind": "assert",
 "assertion": {
 "type": "toolCalledWith",
 "toolName": "echo
2. Poll until status is completed | failed | cancelled | timed_out\ncurl -s \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/
eval-runs/$RUN_ID\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\"\n\n# 3. If it did not pass, read the decision summary FIRST
\ncurl -s \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs/$RUN_ID/decision-summary\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bear

er $MCPJAM_API_KEY"

# 4. Or go straight to per-iteration tool calls, token usage, latency
curl -s "https://app.mcpjam.com/ap

i/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs/$RUN_ID/iterations" \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY"
```

The decision s
ummary composes steps 2 and 4 into one versioned object so every\nclient reads a run the same way. Four things to know before gati

ng on it:

* **`measurementUnit` ships with every count.** Under per-case grading the
 counts are case-execution *variants*, w
ith iterations as trials inside them;\n under a suite-wide accuracy threshold they are trials. The same suite reports\n a differ
ent total under each — 3 against 15 for three cases run five times —\n so a count without its unit is not a fact, and a rate is n

ever converted
 across that line.
* **It explains the verdict; it never re-decides it.** The run's own decision is
 the autho
rity and is carried through on `decision`. The per-trial\n `diagnostics` sit underneath it — a case can pass with a failing trial
in it,\n so tallying diagnostics gives a different answer than the platform reached.\n* **`verdict: \"notEstablished\"` is not a
failure and not `inconclusive`.** It\n means no verdict exists at all (unfinished, stopped early, or undecidable);\n `undecided
.reason` says which. `inconclusive` *is* a decision — the validity\n phase ran and withheld a verdict.\n* **`diagnostics.complete
` says whether you have the whole list.** A page\n fetched with a `cursor` is never complete, and `scannedIterations` separates\n

"nothing failed" from "we did not look".

Evidence is scoped to the claim it supports: for a measured failure the span
id
s, prompt indexes and reasons come from the first failed stage's row alone,\nand `evidence.tracePath` is an API-relative path you

can append to your base URL
to read the full trace.

`model` takes an id from the hosted catalog — `provider/name` form, e.g.
`anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5` — and runs on your organization's credits.\nProvider-native ids (e.g. `claude-sonnet-4-5`) are bring-
your-own-key: pass\nthe key in `modelApiKeys`. A model the API can't execute is rejected at\ncreate time with `VALIDATION_ERROR`;

`details.hostedModels` lists the valid
hosted ids for that provider.

Reruns are even shorter: `{ "suiteId": "..." }` rerun
s the suite exactly as\nconfigured, connecting the suite's saved server selection (the `202` response\nlists the resolved `servers
`). Pass `serverIds` to override the selection; a\nsuite with no saved selection requires it (`VALIDATION_ERROR` with\n`details.re

ason: "NO_SAVED_SERVER_SELECTION"` otherwise).

### Running against a project environment

A [project environment](#endpoint
s) is launchable only through a suite that has\nit **attached**. Attach them first with\n`PATCH /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites/
{suiteId}` and an `environmentIds`\narray (send `null` to detach them all; `[]` is rejected — use `null`), then\npass `environment
Id` on the run. It must be one of that suite's attached\nenvironments; anything else is a `400` with\n`details.reason: \"ENVIRONME

NT_NOT_ATTACHED"`, raised before any case is
authored or any server connected.

Omitting `environmentId` is meaningful, and de
ached → that environment is used automatically. The `202`\n response's `environment` field says so;\n* **several** attached → `40

0` with `details.reason: "ENVIRONMENT_REQUIRED"`,
 naming the candidates.

The environment supplies the closed server set —
including the servers its\npinned plugin versions contribute — so `serverIds` is not required and is\n**rejected** alongside it (`
